newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Megawati backers protest to poll bodies.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Megawati backers protest to poll bodies.

text.p: Supporters of ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri demonstrated in two cities on Tuesday demanding the right to run in May general elections.

Around 400 members of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) gathered peacefully at the General Election Institute (LPU) in Jakarta to protest against the LPU's rejection of Megawati's candidates for the May 29 polls.
In a similar protest in the city of Surabaya, witnesses said more than 2,000 Megawati backers marched peacefully on the East Java office of the election body.

The protests followed President Suharto's warning on Monday of the threat of street violence ahead of the general elections and less than two weeks after the government banned street political parades during the official four-week campaign period.

In Jakarta, only a few police officers were present as Megawati supporters gave LPU officials a letter attacking the election body's approval of election candidates from Megawati's rival Surjadi, who ousted her at a government-backed party congress last June.
"Jakarta PDI members, for the sake of the democratic aspirations of the people, regret the inclusion of the PDI under Surjadi's leadership in the general election," the letter said.
"This will cause the election to have a political defect which in turn will give birth to a government which is not fully supported by the people," it said.
One official of Megawati's PDI faction said this was part of a series of protests across the nation of 200 million people.
Last month, the LPU approved 744 of the 850 candidates put forward by Surjadi in September which included no Megawati supporters. This effectively excluded all of Megawati's backers from the polls.
Suharto called on Monday for the elections to be a "festivity of democracy" without violence.
In both Jakarta and Surabaya, the PDI members took to the streets in convoys of vehicles with about 40 buses, cars and motorbikes in the capital and more than 100 in Surabaya.

Authorities have banned street rallies in the campaign period leading up to the elections for fear of violence. Four major riots have erupted in Indonesia in the past six months, two of them in the last two weeks.
Last July, Jakarta suffered its worst riots in 20 years after Surjadi backers with police support ousted Megawati followers from PDI headquarters in the city centre.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only three political groups legally permitted to contest the elections.
